AI and the Human Factor: Neuroscience, Radical Accessibility (A11Y.md) and Community

The video analyzes the work of designer Felipe A. Carriço: AI accelerates the production of interfaces, but human cognition remains the same. Shows A11Y.md, an open protocol that makes code agents follow WCAG 2.2 AA from the first line, and the AmigUX community, made of horizontal conversations and mentoring.

Published in 30 September 2026 · 7 min 47 s

  • Accessibility and design
  • Technology and culture

Open on YouTube

The video and the transcript are in Portuguese. The minutes between brackets lead to the stretch of the video.

AI exponential, paleolithic brain

The video deals with the shock between technological acceleration and the limits of human nature 00:00. The analysis follows the trajectory, research and philosophy of designer Felipe A. Carriço: anchoring digital development in neurobiological reality, rather than following the blind algorithms 00:20.

The central tension: AI generates interfaces, texts and code at an exponential speed, but the brain that needs to use all this is the same biology of the Paleolithic 00:41. According to the video, this contrast explains much of the digital exhaustion 01:01.

Think of a scale. AI does not tire out and scale production without limit; human cognition has strict bottlenecks of attention and visual perception. If the design only looks at the speed of the AI, the result is mental overload and exhaustion for the user 01:22.

What neuroscience imposes on design

The video cites the research "Projecting realities", which Felipe presented at PUCRS in 2025. The senses and neural pathways of memory are fixed paths: dopamine, consolidation in the hippocampus and the load of decisions in the prefrontal cortex do not change because a new AI came out 01:45.

Ignoring neuroscience is trying to cross the ocean of the Internet through a narrow biological funnel. 02:06.

Felipe summarizes the risk in a sentence: "vibe coding is only vibing for who knows coding". Asking AI to create systems only by intuition, without understanding the technical basis and the human mind, generates noise and broken interfaces. Those who do not understand what is being built lose control of the tool 02:06.

The rule that comes out: AI is a great means of production, but it is not the goal. Filling a screen with dozens of machine-generated components without respecting brain time destroys usability 02:47.

The crisis: climbing exclusion

With AI writing interfaces in seconds, an invisible crisis emerges. AI learns from the current web average, and according to the video, WebAIM data shows that 95.9% of sites have detectable accessibility failures 03:09.

The result is that AI scale the deletion by default: creates buttons that screen readers do not see and confusing forms faster than any team can fix 03:29.

The market treats accessibility as a late checklist, conferred minutes before launch, often due to fear of process. The video proposal is the opposite: accessibility is not final polishing, it is a restriction that exists before the first line of code 03:50.

A11Y.md: accessibility before prompt

To solve this in practice, the A11Y.md, an open source protocol supported by Anthropic's Claude for Open Source program, appears. According to the video, he was also recognized by Smashing Magazine 04:10.

More than a text file, it is a persistent context system: a behavior contract that requires agents like Cursor, Claude and Copilot to follow the accessibility standards from the beginning 04:10.

Inside the agent, the system rotates in four steps 04:31:

1. Loads accessibility context only on demand, so as not to spend tokens for nothing 04:31. 2. Generate the interface already with rigid semantic rules 04:31. 3. Validates the code generated against WCAG 2.2 AA criteria 04:534. 4. Delivers a pending report, so that nothing broken goes on air without human validation 04:53.

The idea comes down to "acessibility before any prompt". Anchoring AI to these principles before she knows what she will build avoids technical errors and ensures that technology breaks down barriers, rather than erecting bigger and faster barriers 05:13.

AmigUX: the collective response

Besides the code, the technological storm brings professional isolation. Mind and well-being only work well with real human connections, and that's where the AmigUX community comes in. 05:34.

The motto is "conversa, not lecture": take out the ego, escape from the stages and LinkedIn marketing, and create a space for people interested in people 05:56.

The pillars are horizontality and empathy, without the owner of truth. The conversations are double-handed, and the mentoring is voluntary and direct 05:56.

The greatest merit, according to the video, is a safe psychological space: a junior or a senior can say "eu do not know how to do this", admit mistakes and evolve without fear of judgment 06:18.

Direct access to other people is the most valuable asset. Each person is a universe of practical knowledge, and the goal is to connect those who want to teach those who need to learn 06:38. This trades like for real professional relationships and creates a network of protection against the uncertainty that the AI causes 06:58.

The human factor as anchor

The technology will continue to accelerate, with new AI and frameworks every month. Biology, the ethical need for accessibility and the strength of a community do not change 06:58. The human factor is the anchor in the middle of the storm 07:19.

The final question: are we designing to feed algorithms or to respect human beings? 07:19

Frequently Asked Questions

What is A11Y.md?

An open source protocol that gives code agents a persistent accessibility context, so that they manage and validate interfaces according to WCAG 2.2 AA 04:10.

Why does AI tend to generate inaccessible interfaces?

Because you learn from the average web, and according to the video, 95.9% of sites have detectable accessibility flaws 03:09.

Reviewed by Maurício Yokoyama Issei in 19 November 2026.

About the video

While Artificial Intelligence has dramatically accelerated the creation of screens and systems, human cognition has remained the same since the paleolithic period. In this explanatory video of 7 and a half minutes, we explore how the work of **Felipe A. Carriço** (Specialist UX Designer, AI Product Builder and Daltonic) connects Neuroscience, Accessibility by AI and Community to ensure that technology continues at the service of the human being.

Learn about the **A11Y.md**, Open-source protocol of persistent context supported by Anthropic's *Claude for Open Source* program that teaches code agents (Cursor, Claude, Copilot) to build accessible interfaces under the WCAG 2.2 AA standard from the first line. Learn also how the ** AmigUX** fosters a " network made by people interested in people", based on free horizontal exchanges and mentoring.
